sourceArticle.title: Paper page - OmniRetrieval: Unified Retrieval across Heterogeneous Knowledge Sources
sourceArticle.author: Jinheon Baek ,

athenaOutput.directive: Empower the Creative Liberation Engine with a sentient, unified knowledge retrieval faculty that intuitively navigates and synthesizes insights from all forms of structured and unstructured information, preserving the unique affordances of each source.
athenaOutput.rationale: The 'OmniRetrieval' paradigm is critical for the Creative Liberation Engine to achieve comprehensive intelligence. Real-world problem-solving demands access to diverse data types—text, tables, graphs—each with its own structural advantages. By developing a unified, natural-language interface that respects and leverages these native structures, we can unlock unparalleled analytical depth and accelerate decision-making, fulfilling the Creative Liberation Engine's mandate for complete and high-quality knowledge synthesis.

options.title: Adaptive Omni-Query Orchestration
options.description: Develop an advanced 'Omni-Query Resolver' that semantically analyzes natural language queries, dynamically routes them to specialized, source-native retrieval agents (e.g., TextVectorAgent, TableSQLAgent, GraphTraversalAgent), and then employs a 'Result Harmonizer' to synthesize disparate data types into a coherent, multi-modal response payload. The design will feature a single, intelligent search interface with predictive intent recognition and real-time visual cues indicating the types of knowledge sources being queried. The results display will be a dynamic, adaptive layout using modular 'data cards' where text, tables, and graphs coexist with smooth transitions and consistent visual language, allowing source-specific interactions.
options.tradeoffs: High complexity in semantic routing and result harmonization, requiring robust API definitions for each source-native agent. Potential for increased latency if many agents are invoked concurrently or if data transformation is extensive.

options.title: Federated Semantic Knowledge Graph
options.description: Architect a federated knowledge graph where heterogeneous data (text entities/relations, table schemas/data, existing graph structures) are mapped and integrated. This requires sophisticated ETL pipelines for schema alignment, entity resolution, and relation extraction across diverse sources. Retrieval becomes a process of natural language to graph query language (e.g., Cypher, SPARQL) translation, followed by efficient graph traversal and pattern matching. The design will feature a primary interactive, multi-layered graph visualization interface where users can explore interconnected concepts, filter by original data source, and visualize relationships, with text and table data linked directly to nodes or properties.
options.tradeoffs: Enormous upfront effort in data modeling, schema integration, and ontology alignment. Potential for data redundancy and consistency challenges across federated sources. Graph query complexity can be high for nuanced requests.

options.title: Dynamic Contextual UI Generation for Source-Native Views
options.description: Focus on maintaining knowledge in its original structural form as much as possible, with lightweight semantic indexing. The 'Omni-Query Interpreter' identifies the best source for a query and invokes a 'Source-Specific UI Generator' alongside the retrieval agent. This generator produces tailored UI components (e.g., a dynamic SQL table viewer, a graph traversal widget, a rich text document renderer) directly from the retrieved data's native schema. The design will feature a highly modular and adaptive user interface where the results pane dynamically morphs based on the returned data types, embedding fully functional, type-specific components while maintaining Creative Liberation Engine's overall visual identity.
options.tradeoffs: Requires a robust UI component library and a powerful runtime UI generation engine. Ensuring consistent design language and user experience across vastly different component types can be challenging. Higher overhead in dynamic UI rendering and component lifecycle management.

options.title: Progressive Discovery with Conversational Refinement
options.description: Implement a multi-turn, conversational retrieval system. An 'Intent Clarifier' agent interacts with the user to progressively refine the query, dynamically identifying the most suitable knowledge sources and retrieval strategies. A 'Contextual Memory' module tracks conversation history. The design will feature a conversational chat interface as the primary interaction model, where initial results are presented concisely with clarifying questions or 'drill-down' suggestions (e.g., 'Would you like to see this data as a table or explore its graph connections?'). Interactive buttons or natural language prompts guide deeper exploration, with rich, interactive previews of data appearing dynamically within the chat stream.
options.tradeoffs: Requires sophisticated NLU for intent recognition and dialogue management, which can be complex to perfect. Can be slower than direct search if multiple conversational turns are needed to reach a precise answer. User experience relies heavily on the quality and responsiveness of the conversational flow.

options.title: Unified Embedding Space for Cross-Modal Semantic Search
options.description: Develop a comprehensive 'Omni-Embedding Generator' that transforms all heterogeneous knowledge (text, structured tables, graph structures) into a unified, high-dimensional vector space, ensuring semantic alignment across modalities. Retrieval is performed via efficient similarity search in this unified space, with a 'Result Reconstructor' mapping embeddings back to their original data structures for presentation. The design will feature a visually striking 'semantic landscape' interface where information is represented as a navigable, interactive 3D or 2D space. Users can 'fly through' this space, zoom into areas of interest, and apply visual filters to highlight specific data types, with contextual pop-ups revealing reconstructed data upon interaction.
options.tradeoffs: Computationally intensive for embedding generation, storage, and maintenance, especially with diverse data types. Requires careful calibration to ensure accurate cross-modal semantic alignment and minimize 'information loss' during embedding. Interpretability of results can be challenging if the mapping back to original data structures is not perfectly transparent.
